title.narrative: Conducive policy and regulatory environment: Strategy

description.narrative: This project supports the continuous upgrading and updating of the Trade and Investment Strategies (TIS) function and related tools and methodologies. It also supports the maintenance of Global Public Goods such as Trade Strategy Map, as well as communications and outreach. Finally, it supports business development activities, leading to W2-funded projects.The TIS Programme is a critical component/intermediate outcome of ITC’s core service “A more conducive policy and regulatory environment for MSMEs”. TIS are often an entry point and compass for ITC’s coordinated interventions in a country, as it systematically identifies opportunities and weaknesses, and defines specific and timebound plans of action for trade development. The process of designing a TIS also builds awareness among stakeholders and structures that increase the chances of successful implementation of identified projects and interventions. In 2022, this project focused on quality, innovation, and business development through network-building. Notable outputs include:On quality:1. The peer review mechanism was reviewed and upgraded to achieve higher quality and more consistency among strategies facilitated by ITC. The NES for South Sudan and Vietnam were reviewed against the new mechanism, as was the sector strategy for Nepal.2. A retreat was held for all export strategy staff and HQ-based consultants, with the aim of re-aligning ITC's work in strategy, through highlighting essential characteristics in process and methodology. This was followed by Trade Strategy Clinics that focus on particular technical aspects of process and methodology in detail.On innovation:3. Research on strategic foresight was conducted, and discussions with ETH Zurich and University of Geneva ensued, with a view to partnering, though funding requests and timelines proved incompatible.4. A new and upgraded user interface for the Strategy Management Implementation Tool (SIMT) was designed and developed.On business development:5. A network of strategy-makers was re-established, and the first edition of the Trade Strategy Forum organized in Geneva. 40 participants from 18 countries shared experiences and debated best practice on "The Challenges Of Implementation", leading to a few requests for support to be funded through W2 project. --------------------------------------------------------------------In 2023, this project continued to focus on quality, innovation, and business development. Notable outputs include:On quality:1. The peer review mechanism was applied to all strategies facilitated by ITC during the time period.2. A retreat was held for all export strategy staff and HQ-based consultants, with the aim of re-aligning ITC's work in strategy. The topic was value-chain analysis and upgrading. This was followed by Trade Strategy Clinics that focus on particular technical aspects of process and methodology in detail.On innovation:3. The new and upgraded user interface for the Strategy Management Implementation Tool (SIMT) was deployed.On business development:4. The network of strategy-makers was established following the first Trade Strategy Forum, and an online platform was launched to strengthen knowledge-sharing. Due to budget cuts, the second edition of the Trade Strategy Forum was to be held in early 2024, so additional budget would be made available through W1 and W2.--------------------------------------------------------------------In 2024, this project continues to focus on quality, innovation, and business development. Notable outputs include:On quality: 1. The peer review mechanism remains consistently applied to all strategies facilitated by ITC, for which staff time is required and must be funded. Due to lower budget, no dedicated staff retreat will be planned in 2024.On innovation:2. Given the focus on quality and business development in 2022 and 2023, and the positive results achieved with the exercise, both in terms of fundraising and improved consistency in strategy processes and documents, priority will be given to revamping the TIS Programme by:- Reinforcing the traditional strategy process through integration with other ITC functions (e.g. TMI's value chain diagnostics, policy's regulatory assessments, etc.)- Upgrading products at the intersection of strategy and implementation, with quicker, standalone interventions in the downstream part of the strategy process. - Tailoring methodologies to support the achievement of ITC moonshots.On business development:3. The network of strategy-makers will continue to be strengthened, and a second edition of the Trade Strategy Forum will be organized in Geneva.
